purpose: Verify that an executable one-body runtime reproduces the passing binary unanimity-28 calculation on fresh neural inference, rather than relying only on saved component decisions.
models: Use exactly the published v9, readout-11 and attention-14 artifacts and their frozen thresholds. Validate all tensor inventories. Readout may change only its active language head; attention may additionally change final-18-layer query/output LoRA tensors. Any other change prevents shared-state inference.
runtime: Capture the frozen first 24 layers once for each input. Compute v9 and readout-11 heads on the original tail representation, then replay the attention-14 tail on the same captured state. Restore original tensors in a finally block. Use the same prefix for all three decisions, and the registered all-three-positive rule. Results expose disagreement and remain unqualified.
evaluation: Fresh inference on all 6002 exposed checkpoints: broad 5022, trajectory DEV 348, challenge 32 and original regression 600. Keep the identical Student03 memory selector, 1200-character budget and complete-turn memory rendering used in parent evaluations. No fitting, thresholds or model selection occur.
verification: Compare every fresh component score with its bound saved parent score, tolerance 1e-5, and require exact component and committee decision equality. Verify actual memory and original input identities. Evaluate in API batches of at most 64 with no padding, no cross-conversation text cache and no old neural prediction reuse.
software_checks: Test all eight vote combinations, invalid and partial outputs, focal-prefix isolation, abstention behavior, shared-state equivalence to full independent models, and restoration after an injected attention-inference failure.
qualification: Passing establishes executable binary engineering parity only. Semantic sets, response checking, independent evaluation, calibration and measured reviewer benefit remain separate requirements.
